q: Which megalithic tomb has a central chamber ringed by smaller side chambers?
n: Passage tombs often have a cruciform central chamber.

q: Which prehistoric structure is a ring of upright stones carrying horizontal slabs?
n: Lintelled stone circles like Stonehenge.

q: Which early dwelling was made of tree branches covered with turf?
n: Branch-and-turf huts were early shelters.

q: Which shelter leans one side against a cave, with stones at its base?
n: A lean-to slopes against a support.

q: The Great Ziggurat of Ur belongs to which architecture?
n: Ur-Nammu built it about 2100 BC.

q: Mesopotamia, where architecture first developed, is mostly in which present-day country?
n: The land between the Tigris and Euphrates.

q: What was the main building material of Sumerian architecture?
n: Sun-dried and fired mud bricks.

q: What are the principal monuments of prehistoric architecture?
n: Burial monuments survive in the greatest number.

q: Mesopotamia is known for which structure?
n: Stepped temple towers.

q: Where are the Tarxien Temples?
n: A megalithic temple complex on Malta.

q: Where are the Olmec colossal heads?
n: Gulf Coast of Mexico.

q: Where are the nuraghe towers?
n: Nuraghi are Bronze Age towers in Sardinia.

q: Where is Göbekli Tepe?
n: In southeastern Anatolia.

q: Where are the Callanish Stones?
n: On the Isle of Lewis.

q: Which burial mound has a long, narrow passage and a gallery?
n: A passage leads to the chamber.

q: Which burial place runs north–south, with a long narrow path leading to an open court?
n: Court tombs have an open forecourt.

q: Which tomb is roofed by slabs laid directly on its side walls, often with outer rows of walling?
n: Wedge tombs narrow toward the back.

q: Which shelter leans on one side of a cave, propped on rows of supports?
n: A lean-to has one sloping side.

q: Which early dwelling of wooden twigs stood on plains or cliffs?
n: Huts were the first freestanding shelters.

q: Which prehistoric tomb has upright stones capped by one large flat slab?
n: A dolmen is a stone table.

q: What is a circle of large stones enclosing a monument or burial mound?
n: Cromlech means stone circle.

q: What is a single tall standing stone of ritual meaning?
n: Menhir means long stone.

q: What is a prehistoric mound of earth and stones over one or more graves?
n: Tumuli (barrows) cover burials.

q: What is any structure of large stones, usually set without mortar, for ritual or burial?
n: Megalith means great stone.
